title: Slide a poster roll into a mailing tube and press an end cap onto each end
instruction: Slide the rolled poster into the mailing tube, then press an end cap onto each end of the tube until it is seated, and let go of everything.
context: Hand packers and packagers (SOC 53-7064, about 645,000 US jobs in May 2023, BLS OEWS) pack rolled prints, posters, drawings and fishing rods in kraft mailing tubes every day. The roll goes in end first and has to travel well past the mouth, because a plug cap is 18 mm deep and cannot seat on a roll that is not far enough in. A cap pushed on crooked or only part way does not seal, the roll shifts in the post, and a cap not seated to its flange pops off in the sorting machine. Real kraft-tube end caps are black plastic (LDPE) plugs with a ribbed, slightly flexible plug that fits the bore snugly by friction (about 3 N to pull out, est), so the cap stays on when the tube is lifted and turned end-down. Each cap is pressed straight along the tube's axis, one at each end.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is z = 0. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and -30.5 cm. (1) A fixed packing board, 100 x 400 mm and 5 mm thick (x 250 to 350 mm, y -200 to +200 mm). (2) Mailing tube, loose: kraft board, 51 mm bore, 54 mm outside, 457 mm (18 in) long, open at both ends, 0.12 kg, friction 0.40, lying along y on the board at x 300 mm, y -228.6 to +228.6 mm, its axis 32 mm high. The wall is a ring of 16 flat staves 1.5 mm thick. (3) Rolled poster, loose: a paper roll 38 mm across and 380 mm long, 0.06 kg, friction 0.40, lying on the table along y at x 300 mm from y +245 to +625 mm, in line with the tube's left end and 16.5 mm outside its mouth (axis 19 mm high). (4) Two end caps, loose: black plastic plugs, each with a 60 mm flange 5 mm thick and an 18 mm deep plug (49 mm across for 15 mm, then a 45 mm lead-in nose 3 mm long) that slides into the bore with 0.5 mm of play, 12 g, friction 0.5. Each lies on its side, axis along y, on its own fixed cap rest at x 170 mm, plug toward the tube: cap a (left) with its flange's inner face at y +345 mm, cap b (right) at y -345 mm. A rest is a 5 mm platform under the plug and a 12 mm rail 4 mm clear of each side of the flange; the cap lies level, its axis 30 mm high. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the poses of the tube, roll and both caps. Roll in: both ends of the roll are at least 15 mm inside the tube's two ends (along its axis) and within 8 mm of its axis. Cap seated at an end: the cap's axis within 5 degrees of the tube's and pointing out of that end, its flange's inner face within 1.5 mm outside the end (2 mm in at most), the flange centre within 2.5 mm of the tube's axis, and the plug's tip within 3 mm of the axis (the plug is in the bore, not beside it). Each end counts once. Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' fingers are 30 mm or more from the tube, roll and caps, and each part moves under 1 mm and turns under 2 degrees. Score 0 if a part is lost (its centre more than 30 mm below the table top or off the table, latched), if the roll is not in, and 0 unless hands off. Otherwise: 1.0 both ends capped; 0.5 one end; 0.25 none. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial, per condition: roll in, before the first cap a depth rod and rule from each open end to the roll's end (15 mm), and a seated cap proves its end because the 18 mm plug cannot pass a roll that is nearer; cap seated, a 1.5 mm feeler between flange and tube end, a 5 degree angle gauge, and the flange's overhang past the tube's outside (3 mm nominal) within 0.5 to 5.5 mm at four points; plug in the bore, a 3 mm tip gauge or the cap not rocking; hands off, a 30 mm spacer against each hand, 30 fps video over the last 1 s and a 1 mm mark on the board; lost, by eye. Real trial only, retention: after the run, lift the tube by its middle 10 cm and turn it end-down, once for each end; a cap that stays seated counts as capped, a cap that falls out counts as not capped. Real trial only, poster damage: unroll the poster; it must have no crease or tear from the packing, or the score is capped at 0.5. The sim reads neither check.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The tube is a 16-sided ring of flat staves, not round, and does not dent. The roll is a solid rigid cylinder for a poster (no bend, no crease, so poster damage is not simulated). The sim plug (49 mm) has clearance in the 51 mm bore: a real cap is a snug friction fit, so retention is not simulated; a seated cap just rests. Caps 12 g (real about 8 g). Stillness turn limit is 2 deg. Frictions and masses are estimates (est).
reset_notes: Lay the tube on the board and the roll in line with its left end at the positions listed, and lay each cap on its rest, plug toward the tube. Real caps and tubes wear: use a fresh cap pair every five trials, and keep the tube's ends round (replace any crushed). Nothing else is consumed.
